ideas.title: Absorption-Ratio Throttle on an Inverse-Volatility Book
ideas.sketch: Each close, compute the 10x10 correlation matrix of daily log returns over the last 60 days and its top eigenvalue share AR60 = lambda_1/10 (the absorption ratio: fraction of cross-asset variance carried by one common factor). Also compute AR20 and the standardised shift dAR = (AR20 - mean(AR250)) / std(AR250). Base weights are inverse-60-day-volatility (risk-parity baseline), scaled so ex-ante portfolio vol is 7%, capped at 100% invested with the rest in cash. The stress throttle is s = 1 - smoothstep(dAR, 0.5, 2.5) mapped to [0.25, 1], so exposure is a smooth function of the stress state (no binary switch) and never below 25% of the vol-targeted book; target weights = s * base. Execution: every trading day move current weights toward target by lambda = 1/5 of the gap, then rescale the step so one-way turnover (half the sum of absolute changes) is at most 3.9% that day, which gives at most 19.5% in a 5-day week by construction; with a continuous target the step is nonzero every day, so trades occur on at least 3 days in every week. Drawdown argument: AR rose sharply into Sep-Oct 2008 and Feb-Mar 2020, and climbed slowly through 2022 as stock-bond correlation turned positive, so the throttle cuts exposure as correlations converge, i.e. exactly when diversification stops working; residual worst case is the loss taken while the throttle ramps (about 10 days to halve exposure under the 3.9% cap), estimated at 8-12% on a 7%-vol book in 2020, with 2022 the binding case because the state rises slowly. Net growth is an honest risk-parity return (roughly 4-5% real to 5-6% nominal after low ETF costs), with the improvement coming from avoiding correlated-drawdown states rather than from forecasting returns.

ideas.title: Stress-Mixture Covariance Sizing with Rank-1 Stress Prior
ideas.sketch: The stress state is not a throttle on the outputs but an input to the covariance used for sizing. Let p_t = clip((AR60_t - q50) / (q95 - q50), 0, 1), where q50 and q95 are the expanding-window 50th and 95th percentiles of AR60 (at least 2 years of history, no look-ahead). Build Sigma_t = (1 - p_t) * Sigma_sample(120d, Ledoit-Wolf shrunk) + p_t * Sigma_stress, where Sigma_stress = D (rho 11' + (1 - rho) I) D with D the 20-day vol diagonal and rho = 0.8: the single-factor 'everything sells off together' scenario, positive stock-bond correlation included, which is the 2008/2020/2022 failure mode. Weights come from equal-risk-contribution under Sigma_t (Newton or cyclical coordinate solve, long-only), then are scaled so sqrt(w' Sigma_t w) = 6%, with the remainder in cash. As p_t rises the sizing formula itself shifts risk toward low-vol assets (Treasuries, TIPS) and into cash, because the scenario covariance no longer credits diversification; the bound on drawdown is stated as a stress-covariance budget: under rho = 0.8 and 6% ex-ante vol, a 5-sigma 20-day loss is about 6% * sqrt(20/252) * 5 = 8.5%, well inside 20% even if the state lags. Execution: trade only on Monday, Wednesday and Friday (next trading day if a holiday), each session moving toward target with sells-to-cash filled first and total one-way turnover capped at 6.5% per session, so weekly turnover is at most 19.5% and there are 3 trading days per full week by rule. Novel element: a stress prior blended in by an eigenvalue-based state variable, rather than a trend or vol signal on individual assets, with the drawdown claim tied to how far AR leads price losses.
